script: The James Webb Space Telescope sits about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. Its main mirror is 6.5 meters wide and made of 18 gold-coated pieces. A sunshield the size of a tennis court keeps it extremely cold. It sees infrared light, which lets it peer through clouds of dust. It has spotted some of the earliest galaxies ever seen.
